main_body: Thatched-roof hut: a large sloped thatch roof (rows 0-36) over a plank front wall with a door, a window and a stone step (rows 38-63)
top_band: Thatch roof slope, light gold #dcb85a/#f0d888 with darker course lines, rows 1-34 (the column scan alternates light and dark rows, so no single clean band). It ends in a lighter eave lip at rows 34-36.
evidence: The roof is a big foreshortened thatch slope drawn in stepped courses, the same way the Beodeul reference roofs are. A bright eave lip at rows 34-36 marks the front edge, and a dark shadow band at rows 37-39 sits directly under it. Below that is the vertical wall face. The door has a dark inner frame and iron straps, the window sits in a dark recess with a sill, and the wall has horizontal beams. The roof and the front wall both satisfy the contract for a building. No isometric side face is drawn.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 6 lightness steps, from #5e4218 through #805c20, #a47a2c, #c49a3e and #dcb85a to #f0d888, with per-course speckle. The outline is a dark brown tinted to the thatch and wood, and 0% of the dark edge pixels are neutral. There is no 5x5 flat fill. The wall planks carry grain, and the door has straps and a handle. Median 8 colours per tile is below the references (18 and 11), and 29 distinct colours is below their 185 and 66. This is partly because the piece is smaller and uses a locked palette. The shading and texture craft are still comparable to the stone-house reference, so it would not look like a sticker beside it.
